questions.stem: Which of the following statements correctly describes a pure substance?

options.text: It can be separated into different components by physical means.
It has a uniform and definite composition.
It is always a solid material.
It contains at least two different types of particles.

questions.explanation: A pure substance has a consistent composition throughout and cannot be separated by physical processes. This distinguishes it from mixtures, which can be separated into their individual components.

distractorRationale.a: This statement describes a mixture, not a pure substance.
distractorRationale.c: Pure substances can exist in solid, liquid, or gas states.
distractorRationale.d: A pure substance consists of only one type of particle.

questions.stem: What is the main principle behind filtration?

options.text: It relies on the differences in boiling points.
It separates based on particle size.
It uses chemical reactions to separate substances.
It involves dissolving materials in a solvent.

questions.explanation: Filtration works by allowing smaller particles to pass through a filter while trapping larger particles. This is effective for separating solids from liquids.

distractorRationale.a: This describes distillation, not filtration.
distractorRationale.c: Chemical reactions are not involved in the filtration process.
distractorRationale.d: Dissolving is not a process used in filtration.
